confirm.text: These are selections made on the air job close-out form, not confirmed events. Technicians should select stop-work authority only when it was actually used, and may be selecting "Unsafe conditions" because they regard wellhead work as inherently unsafe rather than because a specific condition arose. Each item below needs the technician's confirmation before it is treated as anything more. Note that "Stop work authority utilized" was selected on zero forms today — every stop-work selection made was the routine pre-job item "Stop work authority was discussed".
"Unsafe conditions" selected with no supporting narrative on the form:

1099 Alfredo Vaquera — XTO, Tarzan Unit 1 2061DH, job 37361. Also selected "Stop work authority was discussed". Narrative reads "All third-party personnel had great observations on how to stay safe on the job, including hammer swings and forklift LSR".

1099 Alfredo Vaquera — XTO, Scarlet Unit 2 2907BH, job 37355. Also selected "Stop work authority was discussed". Narrative reads "Very good communication between all parties great action plan put in place and all LSR followed accordingly".

1099 Kedrick McCarter — XTO, Morgan-Owens 24A 1H, job 37363. Also selected "Stop work authority was discussed". Narrative reads "We observed a reconnect on the well great communication, everyone performed their task in the safety manner."

1099 Kedrick McCarter — XTO, Morgan-Owens 24G 7H, job 37359. Also selected "Stop work authority was discussed". Narrative reads "A disconnect on the well great communication, everyone performed their task in the safety manner."

Ralph Forbes — XTO, Shackelford 9E 5H, job 37356. Also selected "Stop work authority was discussed". Narrative reads "Had safety meeting went over job scope set up exclusion zone took initial EGT readings."

Ruben Rojo — XTO, Scarlet Unit 2 2907BH, job 37354. No stop-work option selected at all. Narrative reads "A disconnect was made today but once the crew realized we forgot a part, we got to a hold point so they could get the missing part" — a hold point for a missing part, which is not in itself an unsafe condition.

Dawson Drake — XTO, Texas Ten Y PU 3612H, 11:00 AM, job 37350 — this one is not the mis-selection pattern. "Unsafe conditions" was selected and the narrative names the hazard: "A disconnect on a 8000 ppm well". That is a stated H2S concentration and the selection is consistent with it. No action is implied beyond confirming the reading and that the controls matched it.

Two forms where the narrative says stop-work authority was actually used while only "discussed" was selected. 1099 Alfredo Vaquera on Scarlet Unit 2 (37355) wrote "Good stop work authority utilized by one of the employees step back and talked about the situation and continued with task safe safely", and on Tarzan Unit 1 (37361) wrote "Great stop work. Authority was utilized by all personnel." If authority was genuinely exercised on either job, "Stop work authority utilized" is the correct selection and the event should be captured as such. Please confirm with Vaquera what actually happened.

One form where a condition is described but nothing was selected. Luis Zarate on XTO Cheatham #13 (37392) wrote "They tried to grease the master valve to see if they could get it to stop leaking when that didn't work they killed the well and then replaced master valve". A leaking master valve that greasing would not stop is a real condition, and neither "Unsafe conditions" nor any stop-work option was selected on that form. Alexander Clubb, working the same job and well that day (37391), recorded only the job scope: "Job scope was kill the well to replace master valve." Two technicians, one job, materially different records. Worth confirming which account is complete.

Selections being carried forward. 1099 Justin Fontenot filed two air jobs today (Bigby-TXL E15 E 105H, 37323, and Bigby TXL E15 F 106H, 37325) with identical observation lists, identical "What went well" lists and identical narratives word for word ("Safety meeting was conducted and exclusion zones set into place" and "Job went well with zero issues"). Bryan Medlin's two Kathleen Flanagan forms (37352, 37364) share narrative text the same way. That pattern indicates a selection being carried forward rather than made fresh, which is the training point rather than a safety finding.

Previously flagged. Pablo Soto appeared on the empty-multi-select list on 09/26 and again today (see Documentation issues). Michael Jobe, flagged on 09/26 for selecting "Unsafe conditions" with no supporting narrative, is clear on that pattern today.

Trailer Inspection Forms, Trailer Readiness Forms and the equipment sections of the H2S Safety Supervision Daily Inspection Form are photo-based. A defect visible only in a photograph would not surface in this review. Fire extinguisher inspection and expiration dates, first aid kit dates and 4-gas calibration dates exist only inside images, not as text, so this review can confirm that a photo was taken and when it was taken, but not what it shows.

92 of 93 submissions read. The one not read is the H2S Safety Supervision Daily Inspection Form filed by 1099 Marcos Morales at 6:09 PM for Ovintiv St Elmo; its PDF is 26.98 MB, which exceeds the 26.21 MB limit on the mail connector, and it will need to be opened directly in Outlook. Nothing from that form is verified, including its FR uniform answer. Both job boards were available and the 11/25/2026 boards were used; 69 manned rows were checked for coverage, 50 on the Permian Basin board and 19 on the ArkLaTex board. This run started at 11:06 PM Central, before the Central day closed, so any form submitted after that is not in these counts — missing Trailer Readiness Forms are the finding most often resolved by a late submission, and the usual check of the following morning's mail for late arrivals could not be run because that mail does not exist yet.
